identity.title: Phase correction for ALMA. Investigating water vapour radiometer scaling: The long-baseline science verification data case study

paper_type_evidence.quote: We conduct our WVR scaling investigation on the publicly available ALMA Science Verification (SV) observations taken during the long-baseline campaign.

question.value: Whether scaling the water vapour radiometer (WVR) solutions in wvrgcal improves phase correction, coherence and image S/N in ALMA long-baseline science verification data, and how the optimal scaling relates to weather conditions

evidence.quote: We attempt to provide an extra step in reducing the phase variations via the application of a scaling factor in the WVR solutions.
the asteroid Juno at band 6 (2011.0.00013.SV)
Mira at bands 3 and 6 (2011.0.00014.SV)
HL Tau, at bands 3, 6, and 7 (2011.0.00015.SV)

bands.value: Bands 3, 4, 6, 7 (Juno B6; Mira B3, B6; HL Tau B3, B6, B7; SDP.81 B4, B6, B7)

evidence.quote: the young protostar with circumstellar disk, HL Tau, at bands 3, 6, and 7 (2011.0.00015.SV)
The 2014 campaign specifically focussed on baselines from 5 to 15 km.

time_on_source.value: ~1 hr per EB; 75 EBs; bandpass calibrator ~5 min (Mira B6 ~10 min); target scans ~60-80 s, phase calibrator ~15-18 s

evidence.quote: has a typical observing time of $\sim$1 hour.
Typically the on source (i.e. the science target) time for each scan ranges from $\sim$60 to 80 seconds

pipeline_or_manual.value: Data calibrated with the SV reduction scripts in CASA with standard WVR application, then re-run with scaling in wvrgcal

evidence.quote: we first calibrated the data following the reduction scripts supplied with the SV data via casa (cite: McMullin2007) with the standard WVR application without a scaling factor applied.

weighting_robust.value: Bandpass: natural weighting; science targets: briggs as in SV scripts (robust value not stated)

evidence.quote: Images were made with natural weighting with a shallow clean (50 iterations including a source mask of the central 15 pixels in radius)
We also increased the image size to better understand if there is an improvement in the image noise

what.value: Science target imaging parameters (clean threshold, weighting, multi-scale clean) taken from the SV imaging scripts

evidence.quote: These images are produced with exactly the same clean parameters as delivered in the SV imaging scripts for the respective sources

what.value: Initial calibration and flagging follow SV reduction scripts

evidence.quote: These standard calibrated datasets were flagged for errors as noted in the provided SV scripts.

unstated_but_needed: Briggs robust, clean thresholds, cell size, multiscale scales for science images (only in SV scripts)
Exact wvrgcal options besides scale factor
Number of clean iterations used for science images
Which antennas were additionally flagged in scaling analysis

method.value: Extract phases from widest single spectral window of bandpass calibrator and unwrap

evidence.quote: our algorithm extracts the visibilities (i.e. phases) from only the averaged solution of the widest single spectral window from the dataset

validation.value: Diagnostic plots checked per four baselines to catch wrong unwraps

evidence.quote: these plots allow the user to check the phase streams and two-point-deviation profiles for subsets of four baselines per figure.

method.value: Apply standard WVR solutions scaled by a range of factors to raw phases (via unity point-source dataset) and minimise the two-point-deviation of corrected phases

evidence.quote: Our algorithm searches for the WVR scaling factor associated with the lowest TPD of the corrected phases

key_parameters.value: T = 6, 12, 32, 64 s; scale range 0.05-2.5, step 0.01; reference-antenna-only or all baselines

evidence.quote: The range of the scaling values is capped between 0.05 and 2.5 with the smallest scaling increment of 0.01.

fitting.value: Grid search, refined within narrower range, minimising overlapping two-point deviation

evidence.quote: Our algorithm searches for the WVR scaling factor associated with the lowest TPD of the corrected phases, i.e. those with the lowest fluctuations, and further acts to re-adjust the WVR scaling factor (within a narrower range)

validation.value: Reference-antenna-only results compared with all-baseline results

evidence.quote: They are also coincident between those found using baselines with the reference antenna only and those found while assessing all baselines

method.value: Coherence from exp(-phi_rms^2/2) using phase RMS over 60 s and full bandpass; ratio of scaled to standard WVR

evidence.quote: The coherence is calculated from Equation [\[eqn0\]](#eqn0) for each baseline via the phase RMS.
where $\phi_{rms}$ (in radians) is assumed to be Gaussian random phase noise occurring during the observations of the targeted source

method.value: Spearman rank correlation of scaling factors against weather parameters

evidence.quote: The Spearman rank correlation coefficients ($\rho$) are $-$0.38, $-$0.39, and $-$0.76 for pressure, temperature, and PWV

evidence.loc: Water vapour radiometer scaling relationship with conditions
evidence.quote: For the 75 datasets a correlation $\rho$ of $\pm$0.355 is significant at the 99.9 percent level (Table 3 of (cite: Ramsey1989))

analysis_steps.goal: Image bandpass and science targets with and without scaling

method.value: Re-run reduction with scaling in wvrgcal; compare peak flux (dirty) and S/N (cleaned) of scaled vs standard

evidence.quote: Subsequently the delivered reduction scripts were edited to implement the scaling in the wvrgcal routine and then re-run.

validation.value: Same number of clean iterations for both images; noise measured in same regions

evidence.quote: We clean automatically to allow each image made with the normal WVR or scaled WVR calibrated data to be cleaned by the same number of iterations
following the reduction scripts supplied with the SV data via casa

used_for.value: Computing WVR phase solutions with scale factor

evidence.quote: The scale factor is introduced in the wvrgcal code

used_for.value: Phase extraction, TPD statistics and scaling optimisation

evidence.quote: are fully automated in our python package created for the ALMA community
There are 62 EBs of the 75 that indicate the TPD statistic of the phase fluctuation is improved
39 of the total 75 EBs, have a coherence improvement

results_numeric.quantity: EBs with coherence improvement over 60 s

evidence.quote: only 12 EBs indicate there is an improvement on shorter timescales

results_numeric.quantity: Optimal scaling factor range (6 and 12 s)

evidence.quote: The scaling factors we find vary from $\sim$0.6 to $\sim$2.0 for ($T$= 6 and 12 s).
$-$0.38, $-$0.39, and $-$0.76 for pressure, temperature, and PWV, respectively
there are 33 that have image improvements (25 of these $>$5%)
a reduced number of 23 show science target image improvements, in terms of S/N.

results_numeric.quantity: Scaling factor for EB X760 (12 s)

evidence.quote: scaled WVR solution, factor 1.42, applied to the raw data

findings_qualitative.value: Bands 6 and 7 respond to scaling; bands 3 and 4 do not; scaling larger in low-PWV (<1 mm) stable conditions

evidence.quote: bands 6 and 7 respond to the WVR scaling, whereas lower frequencies (bands 3 and 4), which already have good phase coherence, do not.

claims.hypothesis: Standard WVR solutions are not optimal and scaling improves phase correction
claims.experiment: TPD minimisation over scaling factors for 75 EBs
claims.result: Optimal factor generally not unity; 62/75 improve TPD
claims.finding: Scaling improves phase statistics in most EBs

evidence.quote: Our definitive result is that in most cases the factor for optimal phase correction is not unity

claims.experiment: Compare scaled vs standard images of bandpass and science targets
claims.result: 33/39 bandpass and 23/33 science images improved, typically 1-2% S/N
claims.finding: Gains modest for science targets, larger for bandpass

evidence.quote: For the majority of the EBs analysed in this work the S/N typically increases by around 1$-$2 percent

claims.hypothesis: Scaling factor depends on weather conditions
claims.result: Correlation with PWV (-0.76), strongest at PWV<1 mm; none with wind, humidity etc.
claims.finding: Lower PWV needs larger scaling; cause possibly dry-wet air mixing

evidence.quote: The trends with PWV indicated a larger scaling value for lower PWV data

why_this_data.value: Public SV long-baseline data with bandpass calibrators observed ~5 min allow TPD analysis

evidence.quote: for all science datasets the observation of the QSO at the start of the observations, targeted as the bandpass calibrator, can be used for a similar analysis.

limitations_admitted.value: Bandpass calibrator is not co-located with science target; short observations; weather from a single station; cause of scaling undetermined

evidence.quote: in these SV data we only have access to parameters from a single ground-based weather station data

referee_caveats_inferred: Improvement for science targets is small and some may be within noise
Scaling derived on the same bandpass phases used to assess improvement

evidence.quote: publicly available ALMA Science Verification (SV) observations
